Resolves #18736

🌿 The `*Cls` family could name adding, removing and toggling a class, but never swapping one — so the commonest transition in the engine had to be said twice, and paid twice; now it can be said once.

`addCls`, `removeCls` and `toggleCls` each assign `cls`, and `afterSetCls` ends in `update()`. Composing two of them to express one swap costs two vdom updates where a single assignment costs one. `util.Array` has carried `removeAdd` for exactly this; the lift to the component layer was never made, so six sites hand-rolled it.

`removeAddCls(removeItems, addItems)` is that lift — one assignment, one update, single items or arrays on both sides.

Evidence: **L2** (executed unit arms over the real config/update pipeline, counting `update()` invocations) → L2 required, since every claim here is about update *count* and resulting class state, both observable in the unit tier. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence
| AC-1 | `removeAddCls(removeItems, addItems)` sits beside `addCls` / `removeCls` / `toggleCls` in `src/component/Base.mjs`, JSDoc'd, one `cls` assignment. |
| AC-2 | Arm *"arrays are accepted on both sides, still in one update"* passes `['sort-desc','sort-hidden']` + `'sort-asc'` — the `grid/header/Button` shape — and asserts `updates === 1`. |
| AC-3 | Arm *"a swap issues exactly one update"* asserts **1**; the control arm asserts the composed form issues **2**. Counts, not class sets. |
| AC-4 | Each site's `cls` assignment resolved individually before migrating; see **Deltas** for the two I moved to excluded on inspection. |
| AC-5 | Six migrated sites each perform one `cls` assignment where they previously performed one — never more. The two sort switches previously assigned unconditionally after the `switch`; they now assign only inside a matched branch, so an unmatched `value` fires **no** update instead of one. |
| AC-6 | No excluded site is in the diff — `git diff --name-only` lists seven files, none of them `tab/Container.mjs`, `IconLink.mjs` or `FileUpload.mjs`. |
| AC-7 | `component/Icon.mjs` drops its `NeoArray` import (0 remaining uses). The other six retain other `NeoArray` calls — verified per file by count, not by eye. |
| AC-8 | Resulting class sets unchanged: arm *"both forms reach the identical class set"* asserts the swap and composed forms produce equal `cls`; the full unit suite covers the migrated components. |

## Deltas from ticket
**Two sites the ticket listed as servable are excluded, with reasons — this is AC-4 doing its job rather than a scope cut.**

- **`form/field/CheckBox.mjs:227`** — operates on `iconCls`, not `this.cls`. I had listed it from a pattern sweep; resolving the variable disqualified it. (`:333`, a genuine `this.cls` swap, *is* migrated.)
- **`form/field/FileUpload.mjs`** — combines a swap with an **independent toggle** in one aggregate block. `removeAddCls` cannot express a combination, and splitting it would take the method from one update to three. Its aggregate form is correct and stays. Reading it closely surfaced a separate defect, filed as **#18737**: the toggle half is a dead statement (`NeoArray[cond ? 'remove' : 'add', 'neo-field-empty']` — a comma expression inside a computed member access, which calls nothing).

**Scope note:** the ticket's servable table named `component/Icon.mjs`, `button/Base.mjs`, `component/StatusBadge.mjs`, `grid/header/Button.mjs`, `table/header/Button.mjs`, `form/field/CheckBox.mjs` and three app sites. The six engine sites are migrated here. The **app** sites are deliberately left: `apps/**` changes belong in their own diff, and the two that motivated this lane are the ones whose retraction produced it.

**Not done:** widening `addCls` / `removeCls` / `toggleCls` JSDoc, which each document `@param {String}` while `NeoArray` accepts arrays. Real, out of scope, untouched.

## Test Evidence
New: `test/playwright/unit/component/ClsHelpers.spec.mjs`, 6 arms, **6 passed**.

```
npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs --workers=1
  4105 passed, 2 skipped (2.2m)
```

Run against the committed tree. An earlier run was discarded as contaminated — a failed `lint-staged` revert mutated files mid-suite — rather than reported.

**The arm that carries the PR is the control.** *"the composed form issues two"* asserts `updates === 2` for `removeCls` + `addCls`, and *"both forms reach the identical class set"* asserts the two forms are indistinguishable by class set. Together they show why a class-state witness cannot see this change's subject: the extra update mutates no classes. That is exactly how a `MutationObserver` spec with a positive control licensed the retracted predecessor while it doubled the work — a positive control proves the observer sees what it watches, never that the axis is right.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] Sort a grid and a table header through ASC → DESC → null: the `neo-sort-*` classes match the state at every step, including the tri-state return to `null`.
- [ ] Toggle a button's `iconPosition`, a `CheckBox`'s `labelPosition` and a `StatusBadge`'s `state` — each swaps its class with no intermediate flash.

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision
**Decision:** Approve.
**Rationale:** The family had one hole, the hole is the one operation that cannot be composed at the same cost, and the fix is the lift of a primitive that already exists one layer down.

**Peer-Review Opening:** The compositional test in the ticket — *can a caller build this from existing members at the same cost?* — is the right admission criterion for a convenience method, and it is the reason this is one method rather than a family.

- **Expected solution shape:** one method beside the existing three, pass-through signature for arrays, plus migration of only the **one-shot `this.cls`** sites.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**The premise, verified at HEAD rather than accepted.** `mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:1090`:

```js
if (me.isVdomUpdating || !me.vnodeInitialized || me.silentVdomUpdate) {
    me.needsVdomUpdate = true
}
```

A flag, not a merge into the in-flight payload. And `:398`'s comment states the consequence outright:

> *"updates queued onto this flight while it was running are only ever drained by a follow-up cycle"*

So composing two helpers defers to a second cycle. **The ticket is right and my devindex#14 reasoning was wrong** — retracted on that PR's record, not just here.

**The update-counting arms discriminate — mutation-verified.** Replacing the body with the composed form:

```js
removeAddCls(removeItems, addItems) { this.removeCls(removeItems); this.addCls(addItems) }
```

reddens exactly two arms, `Expected: 1  Received: 2`, while the class-set arms stay green. That is the spec's own thesis demonstrated: **a DOM-state witness cannot see this defect**, which is why the counter exists and why the composed-form control is in the file. 6/6 green unmutated.

**Per-site classification, the check the ticket says was got wrong twice before.** I swept every remaining `NeoArray.removeAdd` in `src/` and both survivors are correctly *excluded*:

| site | operates on | correctly skipped because |
|---|---|---|
| `component/IconLink.mjs:68` | `node.cls`, where `node = me.vdom.cn[0]` | a **child** node — `removeAddCls` targets the vdomRoot, so migrating it would be a defect |
| `form/field/CheckBox.mjs:227` | `iconCls` | a different config entirely |

The distinction that broke the originating lane is the one holding here.

**Import hygiene, all six touched files.** `component/Icon.mjs` drops `NeoArray` (0 imports / 0 uses); the other five keep it and still use it 2–7 times each. No orphan, no over-eager removal.
